punchline: James Allen's rich glutton will pay any sum to be cured, except the one price that works: giving up rich food.
thirty_sec: In As a Man Thinketh, James Allen describes three men. A poor man wants a better home but shirks work and cheats his employer. A rich man, sick from gluttony, will pay a fortune for a cure but won't change his diet. An employer cuts wages for profit, goes bankrupt and blames circumstances. Allen's line: circumstance doesn't make a person, it reveals them. His claim that all suffering comes from wrong thought goes too far, though.
